newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rainbow Chicken warns of more big losses.
newsitem.headline: Rainbow Chicken warns of more big losses.

text.p: Ailing South African broiler producer Rainbow Chicken Ltd will report losses significantly higher than expected in the half-year to September, shareholders were warned on Wednesday.

Rainbow parent Hunt Leuchars and Hepburn Holdings Ltd and holding company Huntcor Ltd said in a joint statement that the broiler industry was currently under severe price pressure, with prices of chicken having fallen significantly.

The main reason for the slump was ongoing imports, amounting to 15-20 percent of annual South African consumption, which are entering the trade at prices up to 30 percent lower than the local cost of production, the companies said.
"Improvements in efficiencies at Rainbow are overshadowed by price reductions, and the loss to September will be signficantly higher than had been anticipated," the statement said.
While HL&H's sugar interests and its Robertsons unit continued to perform up to expectations, the results of Huntcor and HL&H would be negativelty affected by the performance of Rainbow, it added.
The firms said that steps were being taken to address the adverse market conditions and that shareholders would be advised of any further significant developments.

In the year to March 31, 1997 Rainbow's attributable loss deepened to 222.99 million rand from 159.81 million a year ago -- well below analysts' expectations and weighing heavily on HLH's year results. No dividend was declared.
